t: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Marine Corps Reserve on active duty under section 10211 of title 10, United States Code, or while serving on active duty under section 12301(d) of title 10, United States Code, in connection with performing duty specified in section 12310(a) of title 10, United States Code, or while undergoing reserve training, or while performing drills or equivalent  duty, and for members of the Marine Corps platoon leaders class, and expenses authorized by section 16131 of title 10, United States Code; and for payments to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund; $378,151,000.

fable.w: This section is a pure appropriation of funds for pay, allowances, and related expenses of Marine Corps Reserve personnel. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision; there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No tempting contrary reading exists beyond the appearance of personnel-related terms, which describe federal service members, not outside participants.

opus.w: This section only sets aside $378,151,000 for Marine Corps Reserve pay, allowances, travel, and related expenses. It does not involve any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. Like Example 1, it just says what funds may be used for, so it does not count as participation.
opus.b: The only tempting reading is to treat the "platoon leaders class" or the payments to the Military Retirement Fund as some kind of process. That doesn't hold up: this is a plain appropriation of money, with no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation provision authorizing funds for the pay and expenses of military personnel (Marine Corps Reserve) and payments to a retirement fund. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government in any decision-making process. The actors involved are federal employees (military personnel) and federal agencies.
qwen_chat.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Marine Corps Reserve on active duty... and for payments to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund; $378,151,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "personnel of the Marine Corps Reserve" are outside the federal government because they are reservists. However, when on active duty or undergoing training as described, they are acting as federal employees/military personnel. The section is purely an appropriation for their pay and expenses, not a mechanism for public consultation or participation in decision-making.
